NRE_note: Per-print setup and material-changeover time are costed at the labour rate (Eq. 12), but design, CAD, file preparation and other one-time engineering are not included; the model starts from slicer G-code (UPEI PDF).
Production_note: Per-part cost is built up from machine time, electricity, material adjusted for shrinkage, wash and sinter post-processing and labour, plus overhead and markup, for the metal BPE route (UPEI PDF, Eqs. 1-16).
QA_Qual_note: The full paper has no qualification, certification or first-article cost term (UPEI PDF).
QA_Insp_note: The full paper has no inspection, testing or quality-control cost term (UPEI PDF).
Storage_note: The full paper does not address inventory or storage (UPEI PDF).
Shared_Capital_note: The hourly machine rate spreads purchase cost over a payback period in months, 21.5 working days per month and a user-set operating hours per day, which is a utilisation input; batch packing enters only through wash and sinter efficiency factors (UPEI PDF, Eqs. 6-7, 11).
Shared_Capacity_note: The full paper costs single parts on one machine and does not address shared or pooled capacity (UPEI PDF).
Speed_note: Print time is computed (from slicer G-code for FFF, scaled by speed, layer and nozzle ratios for BPE) and drives machine cost, but lead time or availability is not calculated (UPEI PDF, Eqs. 12-16).

name: Reiher et al. (Paderborn DMRC) holistic approach: part selection through test and verification
developer: T. Reiher, C. Lindemann, U. Jahnke, G. Deppe, R. Koch (Paderborn University, DMRC)
description: Chains the TOM selection matrix (rough cost quote, knock-out criteria, scored sub-criteria) with topology-optimisation redesign, a manufacturing strategy (orientation, supports, thermal stress) and part marking. It adds a three-tier test scheme: part-independent material/process tests, witness specimens in every build, and part-specific NDT (CT, dimensional, surface) plus load tests. The bracket was 60% lighter with buy-to-fly reduced from ~50 to 1.5. AM was cheaper at the forecast volume, although post-processing and quality costs 'had a major impact'.
NRE_note: A redesign workflow is defined (system-context review, InfoForms, FE topology optimisation, voxel smoothing, NURBS re-intersection with the original CAD), but its effort is not costed (Springer full text).
Production_note: TOM computes a rough cost quote from quantities, current production cost, size, mass and material with depreciation-time and demand assumptions, and a costing tool compares production, self- and lifecycle costs, but the cost build-up and figures are not published (Springer full text).
QA_Qual_note: Prescribes part-independent material/process tests (tensile, SCC, crack growth, fatigue, powder checks), frozen parameters and SOPs, and part-specific tests at qualification loads, with no counts by class and no costs (Springer full text).
QA_Insp_note: Requires witness specimens in every build (at least tensile and density) and part-specific CT, dimensional and surface checks; quality costs are said to have 'a major impact' but are not itemised (Springer full text).
Storage_note: States that only raw material needs storing, reducing inventory, WIP and capital lock-up, and proposes on-demand JIT production at the assembly point, without quantification (Springer full text).
Shared_Capital_note: TOM's rough quote is calculated with depreciation-time and demand assumptions, and high machine prices are said to favour centralised production at almost full workload, but how capital is spread is not documented (Springer full text).
Shared_Capacity_note: Discusses centralised vs distributed production: distributed sites need cheaper machines and more suitable parts, and low build rates require a small buffer inventory; nothing is modelled (Springer full text).
Speed_note: Claims on-demand JIT production can shorten overall lead time for the bracket, with no lead-time values (Springer full text).

name: Siller et al. (TU Berlin) potential-assessment and adaptation method for AM of conventionally made components
developer: N. Siller, S. Werner, V. Molina, D. Göhlich (Technische Universität Berlin, Institute of Machine Design and Systems Technology)
description: A pass/fail prefilter (fits build space, material available, AM-sensitive features acceptable, no legal restriction, conventional production not much cheaper) is followed by 0-4 scored assessments. These cover in-process and post-process restrictions and 'opportunistic' economic, eco-social and functional drivers, weighted by utility analysis. An automatic 'AM adaptation potential' flags parts that minor redesign could make suitable. Below 40% overall means low suitability; above 65% means generally suitable. In the case, 5 of 11 parts failed the prefilter.
NRE_note: An automatic 'AM adaptation potential' score (high at 6 or above) flags parts that minor non-functional redesign could make suitable, but redesign effort is not costed (TU Berlin open-access PDF).
Production_note: Cost enters only as a prefilter check that conventional production is not significantly more cost-efficient and as a 0-4 'Reduces costs' driver (12% weight in the case); no cost is calculated (TU Berlin open-access PDF, Table 7).
QA_Qual_note: No qualification, certification or testing criterion exists; load-capacity simulation and tests follow the assessment outside the method (TU Berlin open-access PDF).
QA_Insp_note: Post-processing need is scored, but inspection or quality assurance is not a criterion (TU Berlin open-access PDF).
Storage_note: Table 7 scores 'Enables on-demand-manufacturing/build-to-order' (21% weight in the turbine case) and 'Secures/improves supply-chain activities' as 0-4 AM drivers, a qualitative proxy for stock avoidance; inventory is not named or costed (TU Berlin open-access PDF).
Shared_Capital_note: Machine capital is not a criterion; machine performance only adjusts geometric thresholds and build-space fit is a prefilter (TU Berlin open-access PDF).
Shared_Capacity_note: Machine capacity or utilisation is not scored; company capacity is mentioned only for scheduling backlogged parts (TU Berlin open-access PDF).
Speed_note: Table 7 includes 'Reduces lead time' as a 0-4 driver (weight 0 in the turbine case for lack of production-time data) and prefilter P9 asks whether the part can be produced or purchased especially fast; lead time is never quantified (TU Berlin open-access PDF).

name: Bracken et al. (Penn State) Geometry for Additive Part Selection (GAPS) worksheet
developer: J. Bracken, T. Pomorski, C. Armstrong, R. Prabhu, T. W. Simpson, K. Jablokow, W. Cleary, N. A. Meisel (Pennsylvania State University)
description: Paper worksheet that rates nine literature-backed geometric features known to affect metal PBF printability and totals them into a geometric-suitability score. Example components were rated and compared with expert assessments, and preliminary user feedback is reported.
NRE_note: The worksheet is a DfAM aid that shows which geometric aspects hurt printability so designers can modify them and guides the design of new parts, but design effort is not costed (nTop blog; Penn State abstract).
Production_note: The documented scope is nine geometric features scored 1/3/5 and totalled into a suitability score; failed-print cost is cited only as motivation (Penn State abstract; nTop blog; Cayley et al. 2024).
QA_Qual_note: The documented scope is geometric printability scoring compared with expert raters, which plainly excludes qualification (Penn State abstract; nTop blog).
QA_Insp_note: The documented scope is geometric printability scoring, which excludes per-part inspection (Penn State abstract; nTop blog).
Storage_note: The documented scope is geometric suitability of a design, which plainly excludes inventory (Penn State abstract).
Shared_Capital_note: The documented scope is geometric suitability of a design, which plainly excludes machine capital (Penn State abstract).
Shared_Capacity_note: The documented scope is geometric suitability of a design, which plainly excludes print capacity (Penn State abstract).
Speed_note: The documented scope is geometric suitability of a design; no build or lead time is estimated (Penn State abstract; nTop blog).

name: Lawand et al. (McGill/Chalmers/GKN) dynamic lifecycle-cost model for DED remanufacturing (repair/extend vs. replace)
developer: L. Lawand, M. Panarotto, P. Andersson, O. Isaksson, M. Kokkolaras (McGill University; Chalmers University of Technology; GKN Aerospace Engine Systems)
description: Present-value lifecycle cost over a 700-month service period, with nine categories: material, manufacturing (variable plus fixed tooling), transport (replacement only), fuel, replacement labour, failure-probability-based repair, inventory, salvage, and recertification (supplemental type certificate fee). Nested optimisation (MADS) picks the stiffener design and deposition time. Deposition timing dominates LCC, and the optimal design lifespan is 312-432 months.
NRE_note: The nine LCC categories contain no design, engineering or deposition-parameter development cost for the adaptable design; the only fixed manufacturing term is machine tooling (gamma_man, USD 20,000) (Chalmers full text, Eq. 2-11).
Production_note: Material (alpha_mat x weight), manufacturing (USD 3.33 per cycle plus fixed tooling), replacement labour and failure-probability-based repair are computed per design over the service period (Chalmers full text, Eq. 2-8, Table 1).
QA_Qual_note: The only certification term is a fixed EASA supplemental-type-certificate fee (gamma_recert = USD 9,977, Eq. 11); qualification testing, analysis or approval effort is not modelled (Chalmers full text).
QA_Insp_note: Inspection and NDT are not mentioned in the model or text (Chalmers full text).
Storage_note: Inventory cost C7 = alpha_inv x weight + beta_inv x design lifespan + gamma_inv is a costed LCC element, but it is held constant and has no deposition term, so AM's effect on stock is not modelled (Chalmers full text, Eq. 9).
Shared_Capital_note: DED machine capital is not modelled; only a fixed tooling cost and per-cycle manufacturing cost appear, with no sharing or utilisation (Chalmers full text).
Shared_Capacity_note: Capacity, sites or pooled resources are not modelled (Chalmers full text).
Speed_note: Downtime, lead time and availability are not modelled; transport is costed only for replacement (Chalmers full text, Eq. 4).

name: Xu & Feng AM-based remanufacturing cost model (remanufacture vs. new manufacture)
developer: Y. Xu, W. Feng (Cranfield University, School of Applied Sciences)
description: Framework and cost-breakdown structure for an AM-based remanufacturing process, validated by expert judgement, with a case comparing remanufacturing cost against new manufacture.
NRE_note: Pre-production cost (reverse engineering plus data processing, from labour rate and working time) is an explicit cost element, about 44% of total in the slat-track case (Springer open-access full text).
Production_note: Per-component cost is built up from setup, wire deposition and grinding (material, shielding gas, wheels, depreciation, power, labour) and overhead, for repairing titanium slat-track lugs vs. milling a new part costed in SEER-MFG (Springer full text).
QA_Qual_note: No qualification or certification step or cost; expert judgement validates the cost model, not the part (Springer full text).
QA_Insp_note: Quality inspection and testing are not in the cost breakdown structure or the cost equations (Springer full text).
Storage_note: Only costs on the remanufacturing premises are considered; inventory and reverse logistics are explicitly left to system-level analysis (Springer full text).
Shared_Capital_note: Machine depreciation is charged as a function of operating time, with idle rates inflating depositing and grinding times, but there is no utilisation, volume or shared-use input (Springer full text).
Shared_Capacity_note: Capacity is not modelled; the scope is the cost of one remanufacturing job on the premises (Springer full text).
Speed_note: Computes depositing and grinding times (mass over deposition rate, adjusted for idle rate) to drive cost, a process-time-only model; lead time, delivery and downtime are not modelled (Springer full text).

name: Baffa (Univ. Florence) WAAM repair-vs-replace sustainability and remanufacturing-viability model
developer: F. Baffa (Università degli Studi di Firenze, doctoral thesis)
description: Develops WAAM repair toolpath strategies, compares the sustainability of repair vs. replacement, and builds a mathematical model of remanufacturing viability (cost and energy) in closed-loop supply chains. It identifies feasible configurations and the parameters that most affect cost and energy.
NRE_note: The thesis is embargoed until 31 Dec 2026, and neither its abstract nor the abstract of the companion J. Cleaner Production 2024 paper says whether the effort of developing repair toolpath strategies is costed (FLORE records; the paper itself is closed access).
Production_note: Both abstracts describe a mathematical model that computes cost and energy of remanufacturing (hybrid WAAM repair) vs. new parts for steel, aluminium and titanium across three supply-chain scenarios, with remanufacturing volume and share of material preserved as the most influential parameters; the cost build-up itself is not public (thesis and JCP 2024 abstracts, FLORE).
QA_Qual_note: Only abstracts are public (thesis embargoed, JCP paper closed access) and neither says whether requalification of repaired parts is costed.
QA_Insp_note: Only abstracts are public and neither says whether inspection of the repaired insert is costed.
Storage_note: The JCP 2024 abstract compares a no-remanufacturing chain with direct and distribution-centre remanufacturing chains but does not say whether inventory is costed (FLORE abstract).
Shared_Capital_note: Only abstracts are public and neither says how WAAM or machining equipment cost is allocated.
Shared_Capacity_note: The three scenarios differ in how customer and manufacturer interact (direct or via a distribution centre), not in shared repair capacity, and the abstracts say nothing on capacity (FLORE abstracts).
Speed_note: Only abstracts are public and neither says whether repair vs. replacement lead time or downtime is valued.

name: IMPACT 2.0 Techno-Economic Analysis Tool for Selection of Metal Part Manufacturing Processes (Topic 3)
developer: University of Arizona Investment Casting Institute (lead), with PADT and 3Degrees. Funded by the OSD ManTech IMPACT 2.0 call, administered by America Makes and NCDMM.
description: A second OSD ManTech-funded TEA tool, parallel to NIAR's, for choosing a metal part manufacturing process. The NCDMM winners page gives only the topic title and team. It is listed so the survey records that the tool exists, not for what it can do.
NRE_note: Only the topic title and team appear in the January 2025 award announcement and the April 2024 call page gives no topic details; no tool content is public (NCDMM winners page; NCDMM call page; searches found no later output).
Production_note: Only the topic title and team appear in the January 2025 award announcement and the April 2024 call page gives no topic details; no tool content is public (NCDMM winners page; NCDMM call page; searches found no later output).
QA_Qual_note: Only the topic title and team appear in the January 2025 award announcement and the April 2024 call page gives no topic details; no tool content is public (NCDMM winners page; NCDMM call page; searches found no later output).
QA_Insp_note: Only the topic title and team appear in the January 2025 award announcement and the April 2024 call page gives no topic details; no tool content is public (NCDMM winners page; NCDMM call page; searches found no later output).
Storage_note: Only the topic title and team appear in the January 2025 award announcement and the April 2024 call page gives no topic details; no tool content is public (NCDMM winners page; NCDMM call page; searches found no later output).
Shared_Capital_note: Only the topic title and team appear in the January 2025 award announcement and the April 2024 call page gives no topic details; no tool content is public (NCDMM winners page; NCDMM call page; searches found no later output).
Shared_Capacity_note: Only the topic title and team appear in the January 2025 award announcement and the April 2024 call page gives no topic details; no tool content is public (NCDMM winners page; NCDMM call page; searches found no later output).
